text: Undergraduate students must maintain a minimum CGPA of 2.0 each semester to remain in good academic standing. Falling below this threshold for two consecutive semesters results in academic probation.
Students are allowed a maximum of three unexcused absences per course per semester. A fourth unexcused absence may result in a grade penalty or course withdrawal at the instructor's discretion.
Any form of plagiarism, including submitting AI-generated text as one's own work without disclosure, is a violation of the Academic Integrity Code and may result in course failure or expulsion.
Tuition fees for each semester are due within 15 days of the start of classes. Late payments incur a 5% surcharge and may lead to a hold on course registration.
Students living in university dormitories must observe quiet hours between 10 PM and 7 AM on weekdays. Violations reported three times in a semester may lead to relocation or eviction from housing.

Course withdrawal is permitted up to the end of the eighth week of the semester. Withdrawals after this deadline require approval from the Dean of Students and are recorded as a 'W' on the transcript.

Students with documented disabilities may request reasonable accommodations, such as extended exam time or alternative formats, by registering with the Office of Disability Services at the start of each semester.
Use of mobile phones during examinations is strictly prohibited. Any student found with a phone during an exam will have their exam invalidated and may face disciplinary review.
Graduate students must complete a thesis proposal defense within the first three semesters of enrollment. Failure to do so may result in a change of academic status to non-thesis track.
Parking permits are mandatory for all vehicles on campus and must be renewed annually. Vehicles without a valid permit are subject to fines starting at $50 per violation.
